text:
Anya: Quick thread — found routing fallback gaps when routing by tier+region to model variants. Symptoms: tool-calling failures and tokenizer mismatches leading to KV-cache misalignment. Repro in staging.
Samir: Can you paste the repro details and which routes this affects?
Anya: Repro on staging eu-west. Route: customer.tier=enterprise -> primary=model-a (float) -> fallback=model-a-4bit. When fallback triggers, tool_call arguments occasionally become undefined and some responses show truncated tool outputs. Manifest shows tokenizer differences: primary uses `gpt2`, fallback uses `spm`.
Jonathan: Tokenizer vocab mismatch would explain shifted token ids and broken KV-cache keys. We need a compatibility matrix and router guards. Quick sketch of what the matrix should include:
```
variant, tokenizer, max_ctx, tool_call_api, kv_cache_compatible
model-a, gpt2, 4096, v1_tools, true
model-a-4bit, spm, 2048, v1_tools, false
model-a-8bit, gpt2, 4096, v2_tools, partial
```
Maria: +1 on the matrix. We also need telemetry events for visibility: `fallback.triggered`, `fallback.reason`, `tokenizer.mismatch`, `toolcall.error_code`. Console should show per-customer fallback rate, latency delta and top model pairs.
infra-bot: deploy-test failed: fallback-compat-check (eu-west). Detected tokenizer mismatch for model-a -> model-a-4bit (error code 42). Logs: /artifacts/1765432099/compat.log
Samir: For safety, we should prefer fallbacks that pass `kv_cache_compatible==true`. If none available, either pick same-tokenizer variant (lower perf) or disable tool-calling during fallback. Which policy do we want as default?
Anya: Prefer strict by default (SRE wants this). UX: rollout page should show a new "Fallback compatibility" column and a per-customer toggle "allow_tokenizer_lax_fallbacks". Global default: strict (disallow tokenizer mismatch fallbacks).
Jonathan: Router unit tests should verify: tokenizer name equality, `max_ctx >= request_length`, and `tool_call_api` parity. If mismatch, router should reject the fallback (or pick a different candidate). Transforming tokens across tokenizers is risky and brittle.
Maria: I'll own telemetry + dashboard. Proposed minimal event payload:
```
{
  "event": "fallback.triggered",
  "model_from": "model-a",
  "model_to": "model-a-4bit",
  "reason": "tokenizer_mismatch",
  "customer_id": "acct-123",
  "request_len": 512
}
```
Anya: Short-term action: change router policy to only allow fallbacks with exact tokenizer match AND identical tool_call_api. Samir — can you patch router config before the canary today EOD?
Samir: On it. I'll add a guard in the routing decision: compare `tokenizer` and `tool_call_api` metadata. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/router/pulls/872 (draft). Adding unit tests now.
Jonathan: Also add a console dashboard tile: fallback rate by model pair, tokenizer mismatch count, avg extra latency on fallback. Maria / frontend to coordinate tiles and alerts.
Maria: Will add tile in "Rollouts -> Fallbacks" and an alert: if `tokenizer_mismatch_rate > 0.5%` for >1h -> page oncall.
Anya: Follow-ups: Samir will PR the guard, Maria will add telemetry + dashboard, Jonathan will add unit tests and the compatibility matrix file in infra repo, I'll update the runbook with the new canary blocker rule.
Samir: PR posted #872 (draft). Quick question: do we auto-block canary if any mismatch errors >0 within first 1k requests?
Anya: Yes — block the canary. Safety-first.
infra-bot: scheduled canary for model-a-4bit in eu-west at 18:00 UTC. :warning:
Jonathan: Copy. I'll run the compatibility validator locally and smoke the tool-call path.
Maria: tagging @oncall for visibility. :eyes:
Anya: Thanks — let's sync in the 2pm infra stand if needed.
